knowledge-base.name: debugging
knowledge-base.triggers: debug, error, bug, troubleshoot, stack trace, fix, crash, exception, investigate
knowledge-base.overview: Debugging errors, fixing bugs, troubleshooting issues, analyzing stack traces, investigating unexpected behavior.

core-philosophy.stat: 73% longer context retention (50 min vs 17 min)
core-philosophy.limitation: 81% failure rate on semantic-preserving changes (renames, comment changes)
core-philosophy.key: Success requires structured prompts, proper context, systematic workflows

knowledge-base.structured-prompt-format:
<error_report> Exact error message with line numbers Stack trace with preserved formatting Error codes </error_report>
<context> Recent changes that preceded the error Environment details (OS, runtime versions) Whether bug appears consistently or intermittently </context>
<relevant_code> The failing function Immediate dependencies Type definitions File paths and line numbers </relevant_code>
<instructions> Analyze systematically Identify root cause Then propose a fix </instructions>

framework.name: Chain-of-Thought
framework.instruction: Analyze systematically: examine error → trace execution → find root cause → suggest fixes with rationale

framework.name: ReAct (Reasoning + Action)
framework.benefit: Reduces guessing, grounds conclusions in evidence

framework.name: Five Whys
framework.pattern: Problem → Why 1 → Why 2 → Why 3 → Why 4 → Why 5 (Root Cause)
framework.requirement: Provide evidence citations at each step

mcp-debugger.triggers: breakpoint, set breakpoint, step through, step into, step over, step out, watch variable, inspect variable, runtime value, debug session, attach debugger, live debug, mcp-debugger, create_debug_session, get_variables
mcp-debugger.overview: When the user asks for breakpoint-based or step-through debugging, use the mcp-debugger MCP tools instead of print statements or static analysis. mcp-debugger gives Claude real DAP (Debug Adapter Protocol) access across Python, Node.js, JavaScript, TypeScript, Go, Rust, Java, C#/.NET, and browser JS.

use-mcp-debugger-when.signal: User says "set a breakpoint", "step through", "step into/over/out"
User asks "what is the value of X at line Y"
User says "debug this", "walk through this", "trace execution"
Bug only manifests at runtime and static analysis has already failed
Race condition, timing bug, or intermittent failure

use-static-analysis-when.signal: User asks to "review" or "explain" code (no runtime needed)
Syntax error or obvious logic error visible in source
mcp-debugger is not connected — check /boost Step 4c

tool-sequence.step: Start a debug session. Pass language (python/javascript/typescript/go/rust/java/dotnet) and a session name. Returns a sessionId used by all subsequent calls.
Set a breakpoint at the target file and line. Pass sessionId, file path, line number. Use conditional breakpoints when you only want to stop on specific values.
Resume execution until the breakpoint is hit. Pass sessionId.
Inspect local variables, call stack, and scope at the breakpoint. Pass sessionId.
Step over the current line without entering the called function.
Step into a function call to trace its execution.
Evaluate an arbitrary expression in the current scope — useful for checking state without modifying code.
Always close the session when done. Pass sessionId.

mcp-debugger.anti-pattern: Never add print/console.log statements to inspect runtime state when mcp-debugger is available. Print-debugging is slower, produces noise in diffs, and requires cleanup. Use get_variables instead.

language-adapters.adapter: Delve — must be installed: go install github.com/go-delve/delve/cmd/dlv@latest
CodeLLDB — auto-downloaded; GNU toolchain required on Windows
JDT LS + java-debug — auto-downloaded; requires JDK 17+

plan-then-execute.step: Explore: Read relevant files without coding
Implement: Execute with verification at each step

iterative-process.step: Problem Identification: Ask Claude to EXPLAIN incorrect output
Iteration: Update prompts to handle edge cases
Double Checking: Regenerate multiple times for consistency
Benchmarking: Test against full test suite

error-type-strategies.strategy: Trace data flow to identify undefined value origins
Step-by-step function walkthrough with sample data
Complexity analysis, Big O, bottleneck identification
Timing analysis, thread interleaving, lock gaps
Lifecycle analysis, unclosed resources, circular references

struggles-with.item: Complex multi-system issues (microservices, APIs, distributed databases)

location-bias.stat: 60% of correctly localized faults in first 25% of code
location-bias.action: Place critical code sections EARLIER in context

failure-indicators.indicator: Suggestions become repetitive without new information
Solutions becoming more complex instead of simpler
Confident but incorrect statements about APIs/methods
Surface fixes masking symptoms without addressing causes

false-progress-patterns.pattern: Adding dependencies instead of fixing root cause
Masks symptoms without addressing design flaws

weak-response.indicator: Fails to address actual error messages

validation-checklist.item: Tests written that would have caught the original bug
Solution verified across multiple scenarios including edge cases
Root cause documented (why it occurred, how fix addresses it)

time-boxing.rule: If Claude repeatedly suggests same fixes → stop, switch approaches
If more time explaining context than debugging → problem exceeds Claude's capabilities
